check_name: Review failed or missed backup jobs
procedure: Review every protected workload for failed, missed, partial, warning, and stale jobs; separate new failures from already-owned exceptions
healthy_signal: Every expected job completed inside its recovery point objective or has an owned exception
exception_trigger: Any expected job is missing, failed, stale, outside RPO, or has no accountable owner
evidence_required: Backup console export or report plus linked ticket for every exception

check_name: Triage endpoint security alerts
procedure: Review new high and critical detections; confirm device, user, time, containment state, ticket route, and current owner
healthy_signal: Every material alert is acknowledged, scoped, contained or assigned, and linked to a ticket
exception_trigger: A high-impact alert is unowned, crosses a customer boundary, lacks device identity, or remains unresolved past the agreed threshold
evidence_required: Detection details, containment action, owner, timestamps, and ticket link

check_name: Review offline and stale endpoints
procedure: Compare offline duration and last-seen age with approved business hours, maintenance windows, decommission records, and known travel or storage
healthy_signal: Offline and stale endpoints are explained, time-bounded, and either restored or tracked as exceptions
exception_trigger: A managed endpoint disappears unexpectedly, reports stale data as healthy, or has no lifecycle owner
evidence_required: RMM export with last seen, device identity, customer, explanation, and ticket

check_name: Review critical service and infrastructure alerts
procedure: Triage critical monitors for servers, network devices, certificates, storage, services, and site connectivity; verify recovery rather than closing on notification alone
healthy_signal: Critical conditions have a verified current state, named owner, and durable ticket history
exception_trigger: An alert is suppressed without evidence, repeats without root-cause ownership, or recovers only in the monitoring console
evidence_required: Alert timeline, independent validation, ticket, and recovery evidence

check_name: Review failed scripts, jobs, and integrations
procedure: Inspect failed, timed-out, cancelled, partially completed, and repeatedly retried work across automations and integrations
healthy_signal: Each failure has bounded retry behavior, preserved output, and an owner or approved disposition
exception_trigger: A job loops, targets the wrong scope, loses original output, or silently skips an expected device
evidence_required: Execution log, target set, exit code, retry count, output, and ticket

check_name: Check alert-to-ticket routing
procedure: Sample material alerts and verify customer mapping, priority, queue, assignment, acknowledgement, recovery updates, and closure behavior
healthy_signal: Operational signals arrive in the correct customer queue with enough context to act
exception_trigger: A material event has no ticket, lands in the wrong tenant, duplicates uncontrollably, or closes without verified recovery
evidence_required: Source event and ticket timeline with correlation identifier

check_name: Reconcile failed patches and pending reboots
procedure: Review failed, missing, excluded, pending-reboot, superseded, offline, and unknown patch states by customer and ring
healthy_signal: Every noncompliant state is explained, assigned, scheduled, excepted, or closed with evidence
exception_trigger: A required update is missing without a ticket, a reboot ages past policy, or the platform reports compliance contrary to endpoint evidence
evidence_required: Patch export, endpoint evidence, exception record, ticket, and next action

check_name: Review noisy, duplicate, and suppressed alerts
procedure: Rank recurring alerts by volume and technician effort; inspect thresholds, deduplication, maintenance windows, dependencies, and recovery rules
healthy_signal: High-volume alerts are actionable or have a measured tuning plan that preserves material detection
exception_trigger: Suppression hides distinct events, maintenance windows remain open, or technicians routinely ignore the signal
evidence_required: Alert-volume report, tuning decision, change approval, and before-after result

check_name: Reconcile unmanaged and duplicate endpoints
procedure: Compare RMM inventory with directory, security, network, procurement, and current customer records; investigate one-source-only and duplicate identities
healthy_signal: Every in-scope endpoint has one durable identity, correct customer placement, and an explained management state
exception_trigger: An endpoint is unmanaged, duplicated, assigned to the wrong tenant, or absent from the expected source
evidence_required: Cross-source exception list, device identifiers, owner, and remediation ticket
system_of_record: RMM and CMDB or asset register

check_name: Review backup capacity and retention warnings
procedure: Inspect repository capacity, immutability or lock state where applicable, retention execution, expiring credentials, and warning trends
healthy_signal: Capacity and retention remain inside approved thresholds with enough lead time for remediation
exception_trigger: Capacity threatens the next backup cycle, retention is shorter than agreed, or immutable copies are unexpectedly absent
evidence_required: Capacity trend, retention configuration, warning history, and ticket

check_name: Review unresolved security and vulnerability work
procedure: Reconcile high-risk findings, aged detections, remediation failures, accepted risks, and evidence of compensating controls
healthy_signal: Each material finding is remediated, time-bound, accepted by the right owner, or actively scheduled
exception_trigger: A high-risk finding is unowned, past due, repeatedly reopened, or marked resolved without evidence
evidence_required: Finding export, risk owner, due date, ticket, and validation result

check_name: Sample automation targeting and outcomes
procedure: Select recent privileged or broad-scope automations; compare approved targets, content version, operator, result, failures, and rollback evidence
healthy_signal: Executed work matches the approved target set and leaves attributable evidence
exception_trigger: An unapproved target ran, script content cannot be identified, or failures lack preserved output
evidence_required: Approval, script hash or version, target preview, execution result, and rollback record

check_name: Review recurring device-health exceptions
procedure: Group repeated disk, memory, service, crash, encryption, battery, and performance exceptions by device and root cause
healthy_signal: Recurring exceptions become owned remediation work rather than repeated alert closure
exception_trigger: The same condition reopens without a problem owner or device replacement decision
evidence_required: Trend report, affected devices, problem record, owner, and target date

check_name: Reconcile material changes into documentation
procedure: Review completed changes, new devices, network changes, vendor contacts, recovery steps, and known exceptions; update approved documentation without storing secrets in the checklist
healthy_signal: Technicians can support the current environment from dated, attributable records
exception_trigger: A production change is absent from documentation or a secret is copied into an inappropriate system
evidence_required: Changed-record list, source tickets, reviewer, and revision timestamp

check_name: Perform and verify a representative restore test
procedure: Select a rotating representative workload; restore to an isolated approved location; verify integrity, usability, timing, permissions, and cleanup
healthy_signal: The restored data or system is usable inside the agreed recovery objective and the test leaves evidence
exception_trigger: A restore cannot complete, exceeds the objective, exposes production data, or is declared successful without validation
evidence_required: Test scope, timestamps, result, validation evidence, cleanup record, and ticket

check_name: Review patch policy effectiveness
procedure: Compare ring performance, deployment latency, failure rates, reboot age, exceptions, and endpoint evidence with the approved policy
healthy_signal: Policy outcomes match approved timing and every deviation has an owner and expiry
exception_trigger: A ring consistently misses targets, exceptions become evergreen, or reported compliance is not reproducible
evidence_required: Monthly patch report, policy comparison, exception list, and corrective actions

check_name: Review privileged technician and service access
procedure: Reconcile named technicians, roles, customer scope, remote-control rights, script rights, API tokens, service accounts, MFA, last use, and employment status
healthy_signal: Only justified current identities retain the least privilege needed for approved work
exception_trigger: Orphaned, shared, stale, over-scoped, non-MFA, or unexplained privileged access exists
evidence_required: Access export, role matrix, approvals, revocation evidence, and exceptions
system_of_record: Identity provider and RMM audit log

check_name: Measure management and security-agent coverage
procedure: Compare expected endpoints with RMM, EDR, backup, encryption, and other required agent inventories; classify missing, stale, unsupported, and retired devices
healthy_signal: Coverage matches the contracted and approved scope or every gap has an owner and due date
exception_trigger: A required agent is absent, stale, unhealthy, duplicated, or assigned to the wrong customer
evidence_required: Coverage reconciliation, device identity, owner, exception, and remediation ticket

check_name: Review policy and configuration drift
procedure: Compare current monitoring, patching, automation, security, backup, and remote-access policy assignments with the approved baseline
healthy_signal: Every managed object has the intended policy version or a documented time-bound exception
exception_trigger: An endpoint or tenant inherits an unintended policy, bypasses a required control, or differs without approval
evidence_required: Baseline comparison, drift export, approved exception, and remediation result

check_name: Review device lifecycle and warranty exceptions
procedure: Reconcile age, support status, warranty, encryption, operating-system support, ownership, disposal state, and replacement decision
healthy_signal: Unsupported and end-of-life assets have an accepted plan, owner, date, and recorded business decision
exception_trigger: An unsupported or unknown-lifecycle asset remains in service without an accountable decision
evidence_required: Lifecycle report, owner, risk decision, replacement date, and ticket

check_name: Review alert and ticket service performance
procedure: Measure acknowledgement, assignment, resolution, reopen, duplicate, false-positive, and stale-ticket patterns against agreed service targets
healthy_signal: Exceptions are measurable and feed a named improvement action rather than being averaged away
exception_trigger: A material queue or customer repeatedly misses targets without an owner or corrective plan
evidence_required: Service report, exception list, root-cause action, owner, and review notes

check_name: Reconcile managed assets with billing and scope
procedure: Compare active managed endpoints, users, sites, licenses, backups, security coverage, and contracted exclusions with billing records
healthy_signal: Billing and service scope reflect current attributable inventory without charging for retired or unmanaged items
exception_trigger: A customer is billed for removed items, receives uncontracted work silently, or has managed assets outside recorded scope
evidence_required: Inventory-to-contract reconciliation, approved adjustment, and effective date

check_name: Sample runbook usability
procedure: Choose one common and one emergency procedure; have an authorized technician follow the current runbook without relying on tribal knowledge
healthy_signal: The procedure is current, bounded, safe, and sufficient to reach the expected result or escalation point
exception_trigger: Steps are missing, unsafe, depend on an unavailable person, or contain stale credentials or links
evidence_required: Test record, gaps, revised runbook, reviewer, and approval

check_name: Review material exceptions with the customer owner
procedure: Summarize unresolved risks, unsupported assets, recovery test results, recurring incidents, overdue decisions, and scope changes for the authorized customer contact
healthy_signal: The customer receives decision-ready facts with owners, dates, and explicit approvals or deferrals
exception_trigger: A material risk is hidden in operational queues or a customer decision lacks an attributable record
evidence_required: Review agenda, decision record, accepted exceptions, and action list

check_name: Review backup configuration and data selection
procedure: Verify protected systems, selected data, exclusions, schedules, retention, immutable copies, encryption, credentials, alert routing, and restore documentation against current scope
healthy_signal: Configuration covers the approved recovery need and every exclusion is deliberate and documented
exception_trigger: Critical data is excluded, credentials or alerts are stale, or retention no longer matches the agreement
evidence_required: Configuration export, scope crosswalk, exclusions, approvals, and corrective actions

check_name: Exercise a broader recovery scenario
procedure: Run an approved tabletop or technical recovery exercise that includes decision authority, dependencies, communications, restoration order, and evidence reconciliation
healthy_signal: The team can declare, coordinate, restore, communicate, and record a bounded recovery using current procedures
exception_trigger: Key access, dependency, contact, restore step, or decision owner fails during the exercise
evidence_required: Exercise plan, timeline, results, gaps, owners, and retest dates

check_name: Review API tokens, OAuth grants, and integration health
procedure: Inventory integrations and grants across RMM, PSA, documentation, backup, security, billing, and identity systems; verify owner, scope, last use, rotation, and revocation path
healthy_signal: Every persistent integration has a current owner, least privilege, expected data flow, monitoring, and tested revocation path
exception_trigger: An orphaned, over-scoped, undocumented, failed, or unrevokable integration exists
evidence_required: Integration inventory, grant details, owner, last use, test result, and remediation

check_name: Review the maintenance cadence itself
procedure: Compare completed checks, overdue work, recurring exceptions, false positives, technician effort, customer impact, and material incidents; change cadence only with approval
healthy_signal: The checklist reflects current risk, contracts, staffing, tooling, and evidence needs without becoming ceremonial
exception_trigger: Checks are routinely skipped, duplicated, unactionable, or completed without evidence
evidence_required: Completion report, lessons learned, approved cadence changes, owner, and effective date
